'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Battle of Khartoum (2023–2025)|Battle of Khartoum]]
***[[Indonesia]] [[emergency evacuation|evacuates]] 43 of its citizens to its embassy in [[Khartoum]] after an [[Indonesians|Indonesian]] citizen is injured by a bullet. [https://jakartaglobe.id/news/sudan-clash-43-indonesians-evacuated-to-khartoum-embassy (Jakarta Globe)]
***The [[Belgium|Belgian]] head of the EU humanitarian mission to [[Sudan]], Wim Fransen, is shot in Khartoum. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2023/04/19/sudan-civil-war-2023-eu-diplomat-shot-germany-evacuation/ (''The Telegraph'')]
**[[Evacuation of foreign nationals during the Sudanese civil war]]
***Many countries, including [[South Korea]], [[Spain]], [[Sweden]], and [[Switzerland]], announce plans to evacuate all of their citizens or nationals from Sudan. [https://www.cnn.com/2023/04/21/africa/sudan-fighting-ceasefire-eid-friday-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[List of military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War|Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War]], [[Latvia–Ukraine relations]]
***[[Latvia]]n Defence Minister [[Ināra Mūrniece]] announces that Latvia will send all of its [[FIM-92 Stinger]] missile systems to [[Ukraine]], following a meeting with [[NATO]] allies at [[Ramstein Air Base]] in [[Germany]]. [https://news.yahoo.com/minister-latvia-send-ukraine-stinger-194511317.html (Yahoo! News)]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]]
**Seven people are killed after an attack in [[Imo State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/gunmen-kill-five-nigerian-police-officers-southeast-2023-04-21/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Anglican realignment]]
**Leaders of the [[Global Fellowship of Confessing Anglicans]], a communion of conservative Anglican churches representing approximately 85% of the global Anglican population, reject the leadership of [[Archbishop of Canterbury]] [[Justin Welby]] as the head of global [[Anglicanism]] over his stance on [[same-sex marriage]]. [https://www.churchtimes.co.uk/articles/2023/28-april/news/world/the-gafcon-kigali-communiqu%C3%A9-in-full (ChurchTimes)]
*Wreckage of the [[Imperial Japanese Navy]] ship [[SS Montevideo Maru|SS ''Montevideo Maru'']], sunk during World War II, is found after 81 years in the [[South China Sea]], off the coast of [[Luzon Island]]. The ship, which was carrying over 1,000 prisoners of war, including 850 Australian POWs, represented the largest loss of life for the Australian armed forces during the Second World War. [https://www.cnn.com/2023/04/21/asia/montevideo-maru-found-south-china-sea-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Twitter]] drops the "state-affiliated" and "government-funded" labels used for the accounts of media organizations. [https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2023/4/21/twitter-drops-state-affiliated-government-funded-labels (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Eight people are killed and 128 others are injured after a rare and large tornado strikes two villages near [[Naypitaw]], [[Myanmar]]. [https://apnews.com/article/myanmar-weather-tornado-naypyitaw-4c88a0ac164bad2226b33b113b8c61cb (AP)]
'''Law and crime'''
*A court in [[Macau]] sentences Levo Chan Weng-lin, the former chair of the city's second largest casino VIP room operator, to 14 years in prison for [[illegal gambling]] and criminal association. [https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/law-and-crime/article/3217903/macau-junket-boss-jailed-14-years-hk15-billion-illegal-gambling-offences-vip-rooms (SCMP)]
*[[1980 Paris synagogue bombing]]
**A court in [[Paris]], [[France]], sentences [[Lebanese Canadian]] lecturer and professor [[Hassan Diab (sociologist)|Hassan Diab]] to life in prison over the bombing of a Parisian synagogue in 1980. Diab was tried [[Trial in absentia|in absentia]] and he remains in [[Canada]] under the request of arrest and extradition from French authorities. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/apr/21/canadian-professor-convicted-in-absentia-of-1980-paris-synagogue-bombing (''The Guardian'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Deputy Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|UK Deputy Prime Minister]] and [[Ministry of Justice (United Kingdom)|Justice Secretary]] [[Dominic Raab]] resigns from both positions following investigations into claims of him bullying staff members. [[Oliver Dowden]] and [[Alex Chalk]] are selected to replace him as Deputy Prime Minister and Justice Secretary respectively. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/4/21/uk-deputy-prime-minister-dominic-raab-accused-of-bullying-quits (Al Jazeera)]
